answer: Whether an agent books a harbor berth, maps a mesa, or buys a lantern, the marketplace grants it one reputation vote only after it locks a fixed bond for 90 days. Each additional voting identity requires another bond, so creating accounts does not multiply influence for free. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full period, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital even if the attack fails.
